title.narrative: Output 1.1. Increased institutional capacity of employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs)

description.narrative:
Between 2022-23, the Federation of Employers of Ukraine (FEU), the Association of Employers’ Organizations of Ukraine (AEOU) and the Confederation of Employers of Ukraine (CEU) developed new services to help their members in managing the impacts of the ongoing war.
In response to the conflict, the FEU engaged 25 of its members in the manufacturing of humanitarian aid, estimated to have reached 25000 people in need. This helped participating companies continue production and safeguard jobs. To take advantage of the measures adopted by the EU allowing for full trade liberalisation with Ukraine, the FEU set up a Help Desk to aid members in accessing the EU market. Between Dec 2022-July 2023, over 60 companies participated in international trade fairs, resulting in the signing of business agreements with a value estimated at US3.5 million. For future sustainability, the FEU developed a plan which foresees several paid for packages for future users of the new service and a marketing strategy to increase its reach.
The AEOU developed a training service on business continuity and resilience. Between Dec 2022-June 2023, training was delivered to 50 companies in partnership with certified trainers based on the ILO Sustainable and Resilient Enterprises (SURE) Programme. A further 1200 companies participated in follow up training delivered in partnership with qualified consultants, on EU trade regulations and related topics. All materials are available on a learning platform. More in-depth training will incur an additional fee as outlined in the AEOU sustainability plan, which also foresees the augmentation of the service with training on the green transition.
The CEU set up a new service delivered though a platform providing guidance on employment of people with disabilities (PwD). Additionally, a campaign was conducted to promote innovative inclusion practices. The CEU sustainability plan specifies staff responsibilities in maintaining and promoting the platform. The ILO engaged the FEU in humanitarian aid interventions and helped design its strategy of localizing the production of humanitarian aid in Ukraine. The ILO assisted the FEU in developing a service offer which continues to be used by the FEU to approach new partners. Moreover, the ILO supported the participation of 100 FEU members in the UN Procurement and Vendor Fair, held in March 2023. In addition, the ILO supported the FEU in developing an innovative service delivered via a virtual help desk and aimed at providing services to companies seeking new markets and business partnerships in the EU. The ILO supplied highly professional external IT support in developing the digital tool and provided guidance and advice throughout the entire process by revising progressively the content of the platform.
The ILO assisted the AEOU in developing a new training service on business resilience and continuity and provided external expertise for the delivery of first-rate training on a range of specific topics. The ILO provided guidance on the content of the training and best delivery model in the current war context.
Finally, the ILO helped the CEU to implement a new service on employment of PwD. Furthermore, the ILO supported the development of legal research and design of the guidelines for companies and materials for raising awareness of the benefits of employing PwD.
Through these interventions the EBMO staff increased their capacity to develop new services in response to member needs and define the best delivery model. Tailored coaching and guidance provided in the development of the sustainability plans has helped define the most sustainable scenarios for the current services and equipped staff with useful knowledge that they will apply in the future. Not least, EBMO writing skills have been enhanced significantly with their staff being responsible for producing and promoting the project activities, under ILO guidance.
